q: What does IFRS S1 cover that IFRS S2 does not?
title: IFRS S1 vs IFRS S2: what S1 adds
short: IFRS S1 covers every sustainability risk and opportunity that could affect a company's prospects, such as water, labour or supply chains, and sets the general rules for any sustainability report. IFRS S2 covers climate only. S2 adds the climate specifics: emissions by scope, scenario analysis, transition plans and climate metrics.

ul: Requires disclosure on all sustainability-related risks and opportunities that could reasonably be expected to affect cash flows, access to finance or cost of capital, not just climate.
Tells you how to find those topics: refer to the SASB Standards, and you may consider other sources such as CDSB guidance or GRI standards.
Sets the core content for any topic: governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics and targets.

sections.h: The general rules in S1 that S2 relies on
p: IFRS S2 does not repeat these, so a climate-only report still has to follow them through S1.
ul: Same reporting entity as the financial statements, and the same reporting period.
Publish at the same time as the financial statements.
Connected information: explain links between sustainability data and the financial statements.
Materiality judged by what could influence investors' decisions.
Comparative figures, a statement of compliance, and how to handle estimates, judgements and errors.
Scope 1, 2 and 3 greenhouse gas emissions, measured under the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard.
Climate resilience assessed with scenario analysis.
Climate transition plans and climate targets.
Cross-industry climate metrics, such as assets exposed to transition and physical risk, internal carbon prices and climate-linked pay.
Industry-based climate metrics, with guidance drawn from SASB.

p: In the first annual reporting period, IFRS S1 Appendix E lets a company report only on climate, applying S2, and leave other sustainability topics for later. Many first-time reporters use it. From the second year the full S1 scope applies, so a company should know by then which non-climate topics are material.

senseible: Senseible does not prepare IFRS S1 or S2 reports. It supplies document-backed Scope 1 and 2 figures from your invoices and bills, which feed the emissions part of IFRS S2.
